title: Shipped a cozy farming game to Google Play in ~11 days with Claude Code + Codex, here's how the workflow looked
author: redrick555
selftext:
I’m a big Stardew Valley fan and wanted to see how far I could get with AI coding agents on a real, finished game, not a prototype. The result is Lantern Acres, a night-time farming game with friendly monster neighbours (ghost mayor, shy vampire baker, quiet werewolf smith). It’s live on Google Play now, first 8 nights free:

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.nodplay.lanternacres

Some numbers and how it was built:

* Stack: TypeScript, Phaser 3, Vite, Capacitor for Android, Electron for an upcoming Steam build
* About 11 days from first commit to store release, around 1000 commits
* I did the game idea, the characters, the design direction and a lot of playtesting. For dialogue I wrote each character’s personality and a bunch of example lines, and the AI built the rest around that
* Claude Code acted as the “lead”: it wrote job briefs, reviewed diffs and screenshots, and decided what to fix next
* Codex did most of the heavy implementation, each job in its own git worktree and branch
* Around 2000 automated tests plus headless Playwright checks at phone and desktop sizes
* Automated “playthrough bots” that play the game from a fresh save and report broken mechanics or missing UI. They found 7 real issues before launch
* Store listing translated into 14 languages

What worked: small, very specific briefs, screenshot reviews at real resolution, and strict rules like “don’t invent extra content”.
What didn’t: agents love to “dress up” a bug instead of removing it, and dialogue still reads a bit AI-ish in places. People spotted that right away.

Happy to answer questions about the pipeline, and honest feedback on the game itself is very welcome.
